headline: Victoria Creates Three New National Parks to Safeguard Rare Wildlife
meta_description: Australia's Victoria state establishes Mount Buangor, Pyrenees, and Wombat-Lerderderg national parks to protect over 250 square miles of forest habitat for gli…
summary_short: Victoria, Australia, has created three new national parks covering over 250 square miles of forest, protecting rare species including greater gliders, powerful owls, and…
body:
Victoria's Parliament has officially established three new national parks spanning more than 250 square miles of central forest, marking the state's first substantial protected areas in 15 years. Mount Buangor National Park, Pyrenees National Park, and the largest—Wombat-Lerderderg National Park—took effect this week following parliamentary approval last November. The parks will safeguard hundreds of rare and threatened species, including greater gliders, powerful owls, platypuses, brush-tailed phascogales, mountain skinks, and unique plants like Mount Cole grevilleas. "Today we get to see the protection these forests deserve," said Matt Ruchel, Executive Director of the Victoria National Parks Association, celebrating alongside campaigners from Wombat Forestcare and the Wilderness Society.

The creation of these parks represents over a decade of community persistence. Wombat Forestcare launched its campaign in 2010 with a public conference in Hepburn, eventually producing detailed ecological reports that convinced the government to investigate and ultimately recommend the parks' protection. "For years we worked with local community groups to search for threatened animals, survey rare plants and, through years of delays, kept writing letter after letter," Ruchel reflected. "Today that hard work becomes permanent protection."

Crucially, these forests lie on lands traditionally cared for by the Dja Dja Wurrung, Eastern Maar, Wadawurrung, Wurundjeri, Gunaikurnai, and Taungurung peoples for thousands of years. Parks Victoria will now join these Indigenous communities in developing management plans over the next 12 months, ensuring both wildlife and people are protected while continuing the landscape stewardship that has endured for millennia.
quick_facts: Three new national parks created in Victoria, Australia in 2025
Over 250 square miles of forest now permanently protected
First new parks of substantial size in Victoria for 15 years
Wombat Forestcare campaigned for protection starting in 2010
